extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, hypotheses, and properties governing the Proj construction, projectivizations, and projective (and related) morphisms of schemes; includes criteria for very ampleness, relative ampleness, and characterizations (closed embeddings into projective bundles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Proj construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Over a scheme X and a quasicoherent graded O_X-algebra S_•, glue the usual affine Proj constructions on each affine open Spec A ≅ U to form an X-scheme Proj_X S_• with a structure morphism β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is independent of choices; works more generally (e.g., ringed spaces or replacing affine opens by any base of the topology). The preimage over any affine open may be computed using the original Proj construction (see Exercise 17.2.C and related exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses 17.2.1: 'finite generation in degree 1' on S
rubrics_metrics.description: Require S_• to be a Z_{≥0}-graded quasicoherent O_X-algebra satisfying: (i) S is 'generated in degree 1' and (ii) S_1 is finite type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make (i) precise by requiring the natural map Sym^•_{O_X} S_1 → S to be surjective. Because Sym^• may be computed affine-locally, generation in degree 1 can be checked on any affine cover. These hypotheses are enforced for the rest of the book, though they may be relaxed if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of O(1) on Proj S under degree-1 generation
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is finitely generated in degree 1 (Hypotheses 17.2.1), construct an invertible sheaf O_{Proj S}(1) that restricts to O_{Proj_A S(Spec A)}(1) over each affine Spec A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.2.D asks the reader to carry out this construction. The O(1) is an important part of the geometry of Proj but (see warnings) is not part of the formal definition of projective morphism used here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj commutes with base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ρ: Z → X and S_• a quasicoherent graded O_X-algebra, there is a natural isomorphism (Proj_Z ρ^*S_•, O(1)) ≅ (Z ×_X Proj_X S_•, ψ^* O_{Proj_X S_•}(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Exercise 17.2.E; the isomorphism identifies the Proj of the pullback algebra with the fiber product Proj and pulls back O(1) accordingly. Use the base-change diagram and the 'top' morphism ψ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: π-very ample (relative very ampleness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a morphism and L an invertible sheaf on X. L is π-very ample if X = Proj_Y S_• for some quasicoherent sheaf of algebras S_• on Y satisfying Hypotheses 17.2.1 and L ≅ O(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a relative notion of very ampleness: L arises from O(1) on a relative Proj presentation. The notion generalizes but is mainly of interest under these finite-generation hypotheses (see Stacks tag 01VM for more general versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Twisting the graded algebra by a line bundle (compatibility of Proj and twisting)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S_• is a graded quasicoherent algebra generated in degree 1 and L is an invertible sheaf on X, define S'_• with S'_n = S_n ⊗ L^{⊗ n}; then Proj S'_• has the same underlying Proj but O(1) is twisted by L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.2.G: informally, Proj is the same while O(1) is modified by tensoring with β^*L; this explains how changing the grading by a line bundle affects O(1) but not the Proj scheme itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivization PF = Proj Sym^• F for a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf F
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite type quasicoherent on X, Proj(Sym^• F) is called the projectivization PF (denoted P(F)); if F is locally free of rank n+1, PF is a P^n-bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction behaves well with base change (see Exercise 17.2.3 and 17.2.G). For locally free F of rank n+1, PF ≅ P(LF) canonically. Special cases recover earlier definitions of P^n_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a projective morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y is projective if there exists an isomorphism X ≅ Proj_Y S_• for a quasicoherent O_Y-algebra S_• satisfying 'finite generation in degree 1' (Hypotheses 17.2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, X is a projective Y-scheme. This generalizes the notion of a projective A-scheme. Note the author's comment that he would prefer O(1) to be part of the definition, but the standard definition used here does not include it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: O(1) omitted from the definition and locality issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Because O(1) is not required in the definition of projective morphism, projectivity is not evidently affine-local on the base; some pleasant properties (locality, composition preservation) require additional hypotheses (e.g., Noetherian, adding O(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate definitions (e.g., Hartshorne's) differ; they agree in 'nice' situations but not always. See Caution 17.3.4 and examples showing projectivity need not be local on the base without extra data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization via closed embedding into a projective bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: π: X → Y is projective iff there exists a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf S_1 on Y and a closed embedding i: X ↪ P_{S_1} over Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.A(a) gives this useful equivalent characterization (hint: use Exercise 17.2.H). This characterization is often used to verify projectivity in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization with a line bundle (O(1) data)
rubrics_metrics.description: π is projective with O(1) ≅ L iff there exist S_1 finite type on Y, a closed embedding i: X ↪ P_{S_1} over Y, and an isomorphism i^* O_{P_{S_1}}(1) ≅ L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.A(b). This makes O(1) part of the data, restoring locality properties under suitable hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivity criterion over a base with ample bundle (projective embedding into P^n_Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y admits an ample line bundle M, then π is projective iff there exists a closed embedding i: X ↪ P^n_Y for some n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.A(c): use S_1 and tensor with a high power of M to obtain global generation and produce the required surjection O_Y^{⊕(n+1)} → S_1 ⊗ M^{⊗ N}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation under base change and relation to properness
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective morphisms are preserved by base change; projective morphisms are proper (hence separated, finite type, and universally closed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that Proj commutes with base change (Exercise 17.2.E) and that projective A-schemes are proper (Theorem 10.3.5). See 17.3.4 for discussion and dependence on locality hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition: projective ∘ projective is projective under quasicompact target
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y and ρ: Y → Z are projective morphisms and Z is quasicompact, then ρ ∘ π is projective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important challenging Exercise 17.3.B: build closed embeddings and use Segre/Proj constructions; first handle the affine target case and then cover Z by affines for the general case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphisms (and closed embeddings) are projective
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite morphisms are projective: given a finite morphism Z → X, one can describe a graded sheaf S_• with S_0 ≅ O_X and S_n ≅ B for n>0 so that Z ≅ Proj S_• (Exercise 17.3.C). In particular, closed embeddings are projective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the chain closed embedding ⇒ finite ⇒ projective ⇒ proper. See Exercise 7.3.J and 17.3.C for constructions and hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiprojective morphism definition (relative notion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is quasicompact, π: X → Y is quasiprojective if π can be expressed as a quasicompact open embedding into a scheme which is projective over Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes the notion is delicate in general and not much used in the text; see Gr-EGA II.5.3 for the general definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative global generation of a quasicoherent sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y quasicompact and quasiseparated and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, F is relatively globally generated (with respect to π) if the natural map π^* π_* F → F is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasicompactness/quasiseparatedness ensure π_*F is quasicoherent (Exercise 13.3.F). The condition is affine-local on Y. There is an 'unimportant aside' noting the definition can be phrased for ringed spaces as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative base-point-freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on X is relatively base-point-free (with respect to π) if L is relatively globally generated (i.e., π^* π_* L → L is surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the classical notion that base-point-free line bundles give morphisms to projective bundles (see Exercise 15.3.5 and 17.3.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative ampleness (π-ample)
rubrics_metrics.description: L is π-ample if for every affine open Spec B ⊂ Y, the restriction L|_{π^{-1}(Spec B)} is ample on π^{-1}(Spec B) over B (equivalently, absolutely ample on π^{-1}(Spec B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L is ample then π is quasicompact and separated; if π is projective, the corresponding O(1) is ample. One can test π-ampleness on affine opens and use Proj constructions even when some finiteness hypotheses fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 17.3.9: equivalent conditions for relative ampleness
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y proper and quasicompact, and L an invertible sheaf on X, the following are equivalent: (a) for some N>0, L^{⊗ N} is π-very ample (equivalently for all n ≥ N); (b) for every finite-type quasicoherent F there exists n_0 such that for n ≥ n_0, F ⊗ L^{⊗ n} is relatively globally generated; (c) L is π-ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise/Theorem 17.3.9 links the geometric notion of relative ampleness with cohomological/global-generation criteria; proofs rely on Theorem 16.6.2 and Noetherian-type arguments (removable in some contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent local criterion for very ampleness under Noetherian hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is proper with Y locally Noetherian and L invertible on X, then L is very ample iff (i) L is relatively base-point-free and (ii) the canonical Y-morphism i: X → P(π_* L) is a closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.G: this implies relative very ampleness is affine-local on Y under these hypotheses (i.e., may be checked on any affine cover). The statement uses finiteness of π_* L (which will be shown under the given hypotheses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample vector bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf E on a proper A-scheme X is ample if O_{P(E)/X}(1) is an ample invertible sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion coincides with ampleness of invertible sheaves when rank 1, and can be checked via projectivizations (Exercise 17.3.10). Properness hypotheses may be relaxed in other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiaffine scheme and morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is quasiaffine if it admits a quasicompact open embedding into an affine scheme; equivalently, the canonical map X → Spec Γ(X, O_X) is a quasicompact open embedding. A morphism π: X → Y is quasiaffine if preimages of affine opens are quasiaffine schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiaffine implies quasicompact and separated. Quasiaffineness is preserved by base change and composition. Exercise 17.3.H gives a useful criterion and proof approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections of PF correspond to surjections from F to invertible sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a locally free sheaf of rank n+1 on X, there is a bijection between sections s: X → P(F) and surjective homomorphisms F → L onto invertible sheaves L on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.2.I: this is the relative analogue of the correspondence between points of projective space and 1-dimensional quotients of a vector space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative projective/affine cone relation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural morphism from Spec S[T] minus the zero-section to Proj S; Spec S[T] contains a closed subscheme identified with Proj S whose complement can be identified with Spec S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 17.2.5: invites the reader to think through the relative cone and its relation to Proj and Spec constructions (see Exercises 8.2.P and 8.2.Q).
